objective.name: continuity.delete
objective.description: Deletes one continuity and its associated mailbox and runtime while preserving the consistency of parent, child, structure, and external historical relations.

#root.role: Remove one continuity from the Brique world, optionally recurse through its descendants, clean every owned operational Matter and relation, and never rewrite history already materialized elsewhere.

effects.continuity: Deletes the target continuity header Matter.
effects.mailbox: Deletes the mailbox Matter owned by the target continuity.
effects.runtime: Deletes the runtime Matter owned by the target continuity.
effects.parent: Removes the deleted continuity id from its parent children relation when a parent exists.
effects.children: Either detaches surviving children or recursively deletes them according to cascade.
effects.structure: Removes every Structure reference to each deleted continuity.
effects.external_history: Leaves messages and effects already materialized in other continuities or external systems untouched.
effects.journal: Deletes the journal Matter of the continuity.

transformation_contract.morphing: An existing continuity becomes absent from Brique together with its owned operational Matters and explicit local relations, while already materialized external history remains unchanged.
invariants: Deleting a continuity never rolls back already materialized external effects.
Messages already stored in another continuity are never rewritten or deleted.
A deleted continuity leaves no owned mailbox or runtime behind.
A deleted continuity leaves no parent children reference behind.
A deleted continuity leaves no Structure reference behind.
cascade defaults to false.
Without cascade, children survive and their parent_id becomes empty.
With cascade, every descendant follows the same deletion semantics.
Deletion never creates a closed or archived continuity state.
A late external result never recreates a deleted continuity.
Active work is not interrupted in the middle of inference, capacity execution, or an individually atomic Matter mutation.
The Matter IDs of a continuity are derived from continuity_id as continuity_<id> (header), journal_<id>, mailbox_<id>, and runtime_<id>; callers never bind them.
A deleted continuity is always removed from the canonical continuities Structure, and the same rule applies recursively to every cascaded descendant.

Mutations of the Matters of one continuity are serialized by short critical-section locks keyed by continuity_id inside the agentic_core wrapper process: a lock is held only around a read, recompute and guarded write, never during an LLM inference, an external invoke or a wait; it is never the sole guarantee.
Every write to a mutable Matter carries expected_revision; a revision conflict causes a bounded read, recompute and retry.
Revision is opaque concurrency metadata and is never used as an application sequence.

Each Matter mutation is individually atomic; the operation as a whole is a recoverable multi-Matter operation with no rollback, whose global consistency is reconstructed through deterministic, idempotent steps and optimistic concurrency.

Locks held simultaneously are acquired in deterministic continuity_id order; a lock of a parent continuity is never held around a recursive call on a child, the state being revalidated when the call returns.

Deletion is a recoverable multi-step protocol executed in this order: children (cascade or detach), parent relation cleanup, Structure reference cleanup, runtime Matter, mailbox Matter, journal Matter, continuity header Matter last.

Each step treats an already absent or already cleaned target as an idempotent success when the remaining state is consistent; the absence of the continuity header Matter marks completion; a continuity header present without its mailbox, runtime or journal is a detectable partial deletion completed by re-running the deletion.
Deleting the runtime before the mailbox and the continuity prevents any new activation, since pilot.activate and mailbox.send fail on a missing runtime.
Writes to a parent or child Matter and to the canonical continuities Structure carry the same expected_revision guard, read just before the write.
A continuity already fully deleted yields an idempotent success with deleted false and no side effect.
A continuity that belongs to a lineage of successions is deleted only with cascade, which removes the whole lineage, newest generation first.
A deleted continuity leaves no reading cursor behind: the cursors of every reader on it are removed before its header, so that a rerun of an interrupted deletion finishes the cleaning.
success: The target continuity Matter no longer exists.
Its mailbox and runtime no longer exist.
Its parent relation is cleaned when applicable.
Without cascade, direct children survive as roots.
With cascade, all descendants are deleted recursively.
No historical data stored outside the deleted continuity is altered.
failure: Fails if the target continuity bundle is internally inconsistent.
Fails if a required relation cleanup cannot be completed coherently.
Does not pretend rollback when some external effect already existed.
Deletion requested during running or waiting is deferred until the applicable safe point.
A partial deletion must remain explicitly detectable and recoverable rather than being reported as complete.
Fails explicitly with a concurrency failure when the bounded retries on revision conflict are exhausted.
Fails when the continuity belongs to a lineage of successions and cascade is not requested.
notes: Executed by the agentic_core Python wrapper.
Physical Matter deletion is delegated to the engine-native matter.delete capacity.
Existing Matter mutations such as parent.children removal and child.parent_id clearing belong to matter.write.
Existing Structure mutations belong to structure.patch.
The contracts of matter.write, matter.delete, and structure.patch were retrieved from the engine and every section that calls them is now formalized.
continuity.delete may recursively invoke itself for cascade deletion.
Deletion order for each continuity: clean parent and children, remove the reference from the canonical continuities Structure, then runtime_<id>, mailbox_<id>, journal_<id>, and continuity_<id>.
The concurrency model of agentic_core is defined once in the document agentic_core_concurrency_model.
Implementation constraint: the in-memory object that duplicates the continuity for performance is evicted with the deletion of its Matters.

#lifecycle.role: Determine whether deletion may execute immediately or must wait for a safe point.

invariants: idle and suspended may be deleted immediately.
running and waiting are deleted only at a safe point.
transformation_contract.morphing: A runtime lifecycle state becomes an immediate-delete or deferred-delete decision.

#relations.role: Capture parent and child relations required for cleanup or recursive deletion.

transformation_contract.morphing: A target continuity becomes an explicit relation-cleanup plan.

#derive_matter_ids.role: Derive the physical Matter IDs of the continuity, its parent, and its direct children from the convention continuity_<id> (header), journal_<id>, mailbox_<id>, runtime_<id>.

invariants: Matter IDs follow the convention continuity_<id> (header), journal_<id>, mailbox_<id>, runtime_<id>.
parent_matter_id is absent when the continuity is a root.
transformation_contract.morphing: Logical continuity identifiers become the physical Matter IDs used by every later deletion step.

#prepare.role: Inspect the target continuity lifecycle and relations and determine the complete deletion plan before destructive effects begin.

invariants: Children and parent relations are known before destructive deletion starts.
Active runtime state is evaluated before deletion.
transformation_contract.morphing: A continuity deletion request becomes an explicit safe deletion plan.

#detach.role: Preserve each child while clearing its reference to the deleted parent.

invariants: Each surviving child receives parent_id empty.
The mutation of each child Matter is delegated to matter.write.

Each child write is guarded by the revision read just before it. On a revision conflict the target is re-read and the content recomputed from the fresh read before a bounded retry; removing an absent value changes nothing.
transformation_contract.morphing: Child continuities of a deleted non-cascading parent become independent root continuities.
notes: Each child continuity Matter is rewritten by one matter.write of its whole content, derived from the content just read without parent_id.

#derive_child_content.role: Derive the child content with parent_id removed.

invariants: The operation is computed from the content just read, so adding a present value or removing an absent one changes nothing.
No field other than the one named by the operation changes.
transformation_contract.morphing: The child content read becomes the same content without parent_id.

#cascade.role: Recursively delete each direct child continuity.

invariants: Each child deletion is delegated back to continuity.delete with cascade enabled.
transformation_contract.morphing: Direct child continuities become recursively deleted continuity subtrees.

#children.role: Resolve descendant behavior according to the cascade policy before the parent continuity disappears.

invariants: Children never disappear implicitly when cascade is false.
Recursive deletion uses the same continuity.delete semantics.
transformation_contract.morphing: A set of direct children becomes either surviving detached roots or recursively deleted descendants.

#parent.role: Remove continuity_id from the existing parent children collection.

invariants: The existing parent Matter mutation is delegated to matter.write.

The parent write is guarded by the revision read just before it. On a revision conflict the target is re-read and the content recomputed from the fresh read before a bounded retry; removing an absent value changes nothing.
transformation_contract.morphing: A parent referencing the soon-to-be-deleted continuity becomes a parent without that child reference.
notes: The parent continuity Matter is rewritten by one matter.write of its whole content, derived from the content just read without continuity_id in children; nothing happens when the continuity has no parent.

#derive_parent_content.role: Derive the parent content with the deleted continuity id removed from children.

invariants: The operation is computed from the content just read, so adding a present value or removing an absent one changes nothing.
No field other than the one named by the operation changes.
transformation_contract.morphing: The parent content read becomes the same content without the deleted id in children.

#structures.role: Remove the reference to the continuity from the canonical continuities Structure.

invariants: Only the canonical continuities Structure is patched.
The existing Structure mutation is delegated to structure.patch.

The Structure write is guarded by the revision read just before it (expected_revision). On a revision conflict the target is re-read and the content recomputed from the fresh read before a bounded retry; removing an absent value changes nothing.
transformation_contract.morphing: The canonical continuities Structure becomes a Structure without the reference to the deleted continuity.
notes: The canonical reference removed is { kind: matter_ref, context: /root/agentic, matter_id: continuity_<id>, role: continuity }, exactly the object added by continuity.create/#structure_relation.

#clean_relations.role: Remove every external organizational relation that points to the target continuity.

invariants: No dangling parent children reference remains after successful deletion.
No dangling reference to the continuity remains in the canonical continuities Structure after successful deletion.
transformation_contract.morphing: A continuity scheduled for deletion becomes unreferenced by its parent and by the canonical continuities Structure.

#delete_runtime.role: Delete the runtime Matter runtime_<id> owned by the continuity.

invariants: Delegated capacity: matter.delete.
transformation_contract.morphing: The continuity runtime Matter becomes absent.

#delete_mailbox.role: Delete the mailbox Matter mailbox_<id> owned by the continuity.

invariants: Delegated capacity: matter.delete.
transformation_contract.morphing: The continuity mailbox Matter becomes absent.

#delete_journal.role: Delete the journal Matter journal_<id> owned by the continuity.

invariants: Delegated capacity: matter.delete.
transformation_contract.morphing: The continuity journal Matter becomes absent.

#delete_continuity.role: Delete the continuity header Matter continuity_<id> itself after owned operational state and external references have been handled.

invariants: Delegated capacity: matter.delete.
transformation_contract.morphing: The target continuity header Matter becomes absent.

#delete_owned_state.role: Delete the target continuity header Matter and its uniquely owned journal, mailbox and runtime Matters.

invariants: Physical deletion of each Matter is delegated to matter.delete.
Deletion of one owned Matter does not imply deletion of unrelated Matters.
No external history is deleted.
The Matters to delete are runtime_<id>, mailbox_<id>, journal_<id>, and continuity_<id> (header), derived from continuity_id, in that order.
transformation_contract.morphing: A relation-clean target continuity bundle becomes absent from Brique persistent Matter state.
notes: matter.delete takes only matter_id; the four invocations use the Matter IDs derived by #derive_matter_ids.

#settle.role: Return the explicit deletion result without recreating, archiving, or closing the removed continuity.

invariants: No closed state is created.
No deleted Matter is recreated.
Late responses cannot implicitly reverse deletion.
transformation_contract.morphing: A completed continuity deletion becomes an explicit final deletion result.
